intentional_differences: SELECT is validated before initialization is marked complete.
BLE/APDU operations are serialized and a timed-out transport requires reconnection.
TX power restoration is attempted on failure as well as success.
No automatic upload of diagnostic logs.
Direct RSP mode remains optional; default is the official Web proxy.
BLE channel encoding is limited to channels 1..3.
After a successful manual notification send the card notification is kept by default; the explicit delete_after option removes it by the parsed notification index (the Web bundle always removes it).

On download notification-delivery failure Python raises a clear 'notification pending' error and keeps the notification for retry; Web v2.3.6 also propagates the failure. The download flow removes the installation notification only on install success, matching v2.3.6 HandleNotification.
Read-only ES10 commands are replayed when the card returns an incomplete chained response.
Chained GET RESPONSE retries an empty 90 00 up to 3 times (a Python-side defensive retry; v2.3.6 readApdu returns immediately on 0x90).
Enable/disable reset the eUICC by default (matches v2.3.6); the API reset=False option lets callers skip it.

ES9+ success is restricted to None/Executed-Success/Executed-WithWarning; the official handleReasonCode only rejects on envelope status!=200 (reasonCode selects the message), so rejecting an unknown functionExecutionStatus is a deliberate tightening.

reset() is best-effort: returns True on any response of at least two bytes (the Web does not inspect the SW, utils:2646-2667) and False on an empty/truncated/no response (timeout/disconnect); it does not auto-reconnect (the official Web registers a 60s reconnect task).

Default ES9+ transport is DirectRSP (own-network SM-DP+ connection), intentionally different from the official Web's default proxy. In the TUI, confirming a proxy download uses the proxy; cancelling it falls back to DirectRSP.

A 200 response with missing/empty data/header is treated as success (matches the official envelope-only check). Download notification deletion is gated on the card's installation result (BPP response), not the HTTP body, so an empty proxy response does not by itself delete the notification.
